key_facts: Primark plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain and has bought a warehouse in Sheffield to ship products to homes; the launch date has not been announced. Before this, Primark offered only click-and-collect (launched in 2022) and no online shopping during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Online accounted for 27.3% of all retail sales in August (year unspecified in the article, per the Office for National Statistics), up from 18.1% in August 2019.

Analysts say Primark's move reflects major challenges from ultra-fast-fashion brands such as Shein; retail analyst Julie Palmer says online sales bring scale and that returns policy can 'make or break' a retailer's online offer.
Some retailers, such as Asos, have started charging a fee for frequent returns; most retailers that charge still offer free in-store returns.
importance_reason: Feature-style consumer piece with one concrete corporate development (Primark home delivery plan) but no market-moving data or policy event.
market_link: Primark's entry into home delivery signals competitive pressure from Shein and online-share growth in UK retail, but no direct price or asset effect is stated.

actors: Dalton Jacobus (Department of Neighborhood Services, Des Moines)
Kunak (company behind monitors in Des Moines)
key_facts: In Milpitas, California, local authorities ordered the operators of the Newby Island landfill to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure odour-causing chemicals, and to automate collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.

In Des Moines, Iowa, city authorities spend around $240,000 a year on a ring of odour monitors combined with a weather station to provide real-time data on concentrations from each facility based on wind patterns; Smithfield Foods says it invested $2m in a regenerative thermal oxidiser but denies being the source of complaints.

The US Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant, leaving states and local governments to handle the issue; many countries have no odour regulations. Best industrial odour-control technologies can remove 90% or more of target compounds when used correctly, while cheaper masking with deodorisers is considered ineffective by odour experts.

Experts say that urban sprawl and rising land values bring residential development closer to odorous facilities, increasing demand for monitoring technologies; the article also notes the traditional olfactometry (human panels) is still common.
importance_reason: Общий обзор проблемы запахов и технологий мониторинга без привязки к рыночному событию или решению регулятора.

key_facts: KFC is switching from Pepsi to Coca-Cola products.
As more people switch to Coke, some analysts are growing more worried about the state of archrival Pepsi.
importance_reason: Corporate news about a single restaurant chain's beverage supplier switch, with limited direct market impact.
market_link: Possible modest pressure on PepsiCo's food-service volumes and sentiment toward its beverage segment, though the effect is likely small.
